War on Buses

By: Jana Marx | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
It seems like rogue taxi drivers will stop at nothing to clear their turf of other transport sectors - even if it leads to killings.

Unique Selling Point:
Actual footage of these attacks happening and people getting shot at or killed.

Summary:
On 28 April 2022 an Intercape bus driver died days after being shot and critically wounded outside the Company’s Cape Town depot in what is part of a campaign of violence and extortion against the Long Distance Coach industry by rogue elements in the minibus taxi industry. The 35 year old victim leaves behind a wife and two daughters.

In the space of just 13 months, there have been over 150 recorded violent incidents targeting Intercape,the country's largest and longest-standing bus company. A number of which have led to serious injury of industry employees and passengers on long distance coaches. The death of this latest Intercape employee comes as the Company has pleaded repeatedly for urgent government intervention to stop the campaign of violence.

Intercape is not the only company being targeted, though, but they have been hit the hardest, because they are the biggest bus line driving long distance in the country. Also, they refuse to pay “protection money”. “Protection money” or “security tax” is money paid to ensure you will not be targeted by criminals. Thugs in the taxi industry try to extort long distance bus lines to either stay out of their “claimed” regions, or pay protection money to not fall victim to the attacks.

SAPS and Nat Joints are supposed to be on board, but the attacks are only intensifying. More than 60 cases have been opened with the SAPS but the attacks have continued unabated at key pick-up points along routes and on the road, as well as outside Intercape headquarters in Cape Town where there have been two brazen shooting incidents, the latest of which was fatal.

Intercape has now written to President Cyril Ramaphosa to act.

Press Release:


The War on Buses 
Long-distance bus travel is a lucrative business in South Africa, with thousands of passengers transported across the country each day. But, in the Eastern Cape, regional roads are highly prized and, for some minibus taxi drivers, not for sharing. When buses “stray” onto their turf, the consequences are often violent, sometimes deadly. A Carte Blanche investigation lays bare the extreme hazards associated with bus travel, and discovers the problem extends into other provinces, too. 
Producer: Jana Marx | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


In the midst of a new and terrifying crime wave…

(SHOTS FIRED)

… a late afternoon prayer for protection.

(SHOTS FIRED, PEOPLE SCREAMING)

Innocent victims are paying the price…

In a deadly turf war.

2 BREAK
3 VO It started out like any normal day. A bus driver we’ll call Joseph to protect his identity, was getting ready for work.
4 VO He was on his way to the Eastern Cape – a route he knew well after working in the bus industry for 24 years.

From Pretoria to Midrand to Park Station in Johannesburg…Joseph collected passengers…

5 VO When he left Park Station he had about 40 people on board.

For Joseph, the passengers always come first.

6 UPS Joseph: 06;11 This thing – it’s like being a father and you have kids, because all those people are depending on you.

SUBTITLES: This thing – it’s like being a father and you have kids, because all those people are depending on you.

7 VO As he approached the highway onramp, his bus reached 98 km/h.

8 (Pause voice but change visuals to inside cab)

9 UPS 14;12 I thought it was a tyre exploding, so I checked my steering wheel to feel if everything was still alright.

SUBTITLES: I thought it was a tyre exploding, so I checked my steering wheel to feel if everything was still alright.

14: 24 Then I heard 2 banging sounds! I realised, haai man, something is wrong here. I saw glass falling as a car passed.

SUBTITLES: Then I heard 2 banging sounds!

I realised, no man, something is wrong here. A car passed and I saw my windscreen shatter.

10 VO Joseph immediately reduced his speed.

By leaning over to the one side to dodge bullets, he focused on keeping the bus on the road.

11 He kept control of the bus by using the reflective cat’s eyes to help him steer.

12 UPS 16:23 I didn’t see where I am going, and I thought if I steer like this – those lights on the street – 16;32 when I heard the scratching sound, I could feel that it was going off the road 16;43 ,

SUBTITLES: When you drive over them, it makes a sound, so when I heard the sound I could feel I was going off the road.

13 VO Driving blind, he kept going.

14 UPS 17;00 Until I heard that the shooting had stopped.

SUBTITLES: Until I could hear that the shooting had stopped.

15 VO He got the bus to safety - his only injury, the impact of the steering wheel when he ducked the bullets.

But the long-distance coach bore the signs of an ambush that could’ve easily gone south.

16 LINK What I’ve just heard does not sound like a bus driver’s story. It sounds like a man going to war, unarmed. The only difference is, he didn’t sign up for that…

17 VO I recalled the gruesome attacks by metered and minibus taxis on e-hailing services like Uber.

The focus may now have shifted to long-distance buses, but the attacks are just as brutal.

18 VO Johann Ferreira, CEO of Intercape, says his company has experienced more than 150 attacks over the past year – mostly in the Eastern and Western Cape, and lately also in Gauteng.

Incidents involve stoning and shootings, causing serious injury and even death.

19 UPS Johann 7;32 So buses are being stoned on a regular basis throughout South Africa, but recently, in the last, say, 15 months, we've experienced a lot of attacks on coaches coming through the Eastern Cape. This is definitely taxi-related.

10;29 What makes you so certain?

10;34 Once there has been talks with the taxi associations, and they perceive that there is some sort of agreement reached, it will stop.

20 VO But he’s adamant he won’t concede to informal agreements, no matter the threats.

The industry is already being regulated by provincial authorities and operating licences are issued under the National Land Transport Act.

Simply put, these buses have a legal right to be on the road, and no amount of bullying can change that.

21 13;05 So the taxi operators would then come to you guys as an industry and say, these are the routes that you can operate on. And you can't operate on here. And you have to pay sort of protection fee for us not to attack you?

13;22 If you're willing to pay the ransom demand, then they will leave you alone.

22 VO “Ransom demand” is an appropriate description. This is like a hostage situation.

Also known as security tax, money is paid to criminals so that they won’t attack you. It’s an arrangement very reminiscent of the mafia… a kind of warped insurance policy.

23 UPS 13;31 And this ransom demand is in the range of millions?

Millions. Millions and millions.

24 VO It seems that there are only three ways to avoid violence:

* Bus companies can agree, for example, to inflate their prices, which is illegal under the Competition Commission Act. This happened during the first wave of the Covid pandemic and companies were brought to justice for it.
* Alternatively, they can cave in and pay the security tax; or,
* steer clear of contested areas and routes.

25 VO In the 45 minutes we interviewed Ferreira, he received more bad news…

26 UPS 0;13 - 0;39 I actually can’t believe this. So while we’ve been doing this interview, Johann, two of your buses have been attacked…

Yes, I believe so…

(he reads from the message till 0;39)

27 VO Because of his refusal to cooperate with criminals, Eastern Cape towns like Dutywa, Butterworth, Tsomo, Cofimvaba and Ngcobo have become war zones for Intercape buses.

28 VO But the reign of terror has extended to other provinces as well…

Terrifyingly, demonstrated by this CCTV footage of an Intercape bus leaving a depot in Cape Town.

29 VO

SHOTS FIRED

Bangikhaya Machana was shot three times.

30 VO His colleague who was sitting next to him, we’ll call him Dylan, recalls that fateful day…

31 UPS 4;55 When they start shooting what's going through your mind?

5;01 The intention was to shoot at the driver.

He was struggling with the seatbelt. That is where he got shot.

06;14 The bullets was flying to this window…

So we jumped up, over and he got into the sleeping compartment.

32 LINK I'm shocked how terrified these drivers were to talk to us... afraid that their attackers may come back and finish them off. They are bus drivers, not soldiers at war.

33 VO Machana underwent emergency surgery in a desperate bid to save his life.

But the young father succumbed to his injuries only days later.

34 VO His grieving cousin, Koleke Machana, recalls that Machana’s love for driving buses took root when he was still just a child.

35 UPS 3;13 I remember they drove a bus without permission. So this is the reason the guy decided no, this child loves this. He took him to the Driving Academy.

36 VO Machana was the family breadwinner: husband and father to small girls.

37 VO Sadly, this mourning family’s trauma was far from over.

When they arrived in an Intercape bus at Dutywa for the burial, minibus taxi drivers prevented them from entering the town.

Their pleas fell on deaf ears and the taxi operators forced them to leave the area.

38 UPS 08:01 We just asked the driver please drive to this Mthatha you are instructed to drive to before we die here. We were scared.

39 VO Mthatha police escorted the bus back to Dutywa.

40 MEMORIAL SINGING

41 VO Intercape has intensified security at its depots and according to Ferreira, unmarked vehicles now have to escort buses on some routes.



42 VO Sadly, when buses are under siege, passengers also pay a price.

On 29 April, an excited Pretty Nondabula, a mother of two, boarded a bus to visit family in the Eastern Cape.

43 VO She could not have known what would follow…

44 UPS 6;44
So you were shot?
Yeah.
Trying to go home?
Yeah.

07;13 What did that feel like?

7;38 If you can put your leg on hot water - the hot, hot, hot, hot water when you're trying to put it like this. It's like that.

45 VO Traumatised and frantic to get home, Pretty’s leg was simply bandaged, before she got onto another bus to finish the trip.

46 VO Police in the Eastern Cape confirmed that they are prioritising investigations into the stoning of buses and intimidation by taxi operators.

No arrests have been made yet.

On screen:

“The SAPS in the Eastern Cape is doing everything it can to prevent further occurrence of violent incidents aimed at buses.”

In the Western Cape, a designated Taxi Violence Task Team and an Extortion Task Team are taking charge.

They say their current investigations are linked to only one bus company, but the possibility that others are affected, cannot be ruled out.

On screen:

“Due to the sensitive nature of serious and violent crimes such as extortion, it is not possible to discuss the finer aspects of these cases on an open platform, as the identities of the victims must be protected.”

47 VO When asked if the issue is receiving attention at a national level, the SAPS National Office did not want to comment, merely saying that the investigation is ongoing.

48 VO Ferreira says he has opened more than 60 cases with the police.

49 VO In the meantime, Joseph bids a final farewell to his wife before every trip.

50 UPS SUBTITLES

I ended up giving the Eastern Cape a name, calling it…what is the name of the country that is fighting with Russia?
Ukraine
I tell her that I’m going to Ukraine and we'll see if I come back.

51 VO Realising that a few thugs don’t define a whole industry, we tried to arrange an interview with the South African National Taxi Council, or SANTACO, but numerous WhatsApp messages, calls, SMS and emails to the official spokesperson stayed unanswered.

But we cornered Minister Fikile Mbalula after an unrelated press briefing near Cape Town.

52 UPS 04;01 What do you do as a Minister of Transport when you have this one mode of transport being the taxi operators, intimidating and coming with arms, guns and taking passengers out?

04;24 Yes, you will know that from our side, we are dealing with a plethora of issues in terms of the taxi industry. And the chief amongst them is formalisation. And regulating.

53 VO This means the establishment of what he calls a “dedicated force”, focusing on violence in the taxi industry.

54 UPS 4;33 but at the present moment, with limited resources we've got our focus must shift to law enforcement

15;18 Where such happens, the minister got powers to close the roads, including MCs in the provinces, and that is what we'll do.

Why aren’t you doing it yet?

05;15 Well, uh,we have done it where there's been an occurrence of that.

55 VO The Minister believes that a joint response by authorities, state departments and bus companies is needed.

56 UPS 05;47 Minister, to the family members of concerned every day when they keep hearing that they won't come back. What do you have to say?

5;23 I'm saying to them that from our side, the Ministry of Transport, we will do everything in our power to ensure that the criminals who are doing this work to book and then we would dedicate ourselves in the form of a team that will focus on this sort of violence.

57 VO All of which comes too late for Bangikhaya Machana and his bereaved family…




PROMOS



PROMO1 - 11 sec

VO First e-hailing services, now long-distance buses…

It seems like rogue taxi drivers will stop at nothing to clear their turf of other transport sectors - even if it leads to killings.




PROMO 2 - 21 sec

UPS 14;12 I thought it was a tyre exploding, so I checked my steering wheel and I felt if everything was still alright.

SUBTITLES: I thought it was a tyre exploding, so I checked my steering wheel to feel if everything was still alright.

I realised, no man, something is wrong here.

VO Innocent bus drivers are getting injured and killed in a reign of terror led by taxi drivers. When will this stop?



PROMO3 - 21 sec

VO Long-distance bus travel is big business and highways from Johannesburg and Cape Town to small towns in the Eastern Cape, are prime real estate...now some minibus taxi drivers are staking their claim and they’ll stop at nothing to get the buses off the road...

UPS 08:01 So we just asked the driver please drive to this Mthatha you are instructed to drive to before we die here. We were scared.

The focus may now have shifted to long-distance buses, but the attacks are just as brutal. 18 VO Johann Ferreira, CEO of Intercape, says his company has experienced more than 150 attacks over the past year – mostly in the Eastern and Western Cape, and lately also in Gauteng. Incidents involve stoning and shootings, causing serious injury and even death. 19 UPS Johann 7;32 So buses are being stoned on a regular basis throughout South Africa, but recently, in the last, say, 15 months, we've experienced a lot of attacks on coaches coming through the Eastern Cape. This is definitely taxi-related. 10;29 What makes you so certain? 10;34 Once there has been talks with the taxi associations, and they perceive that there is some sort of agreement reached, it will stop. 20 VO But he’s adamant he won’t concede to informal agreements, no matter the threats. The industry is already being regulated by provincial authorities and operating licences are issued under the National Land Transport Act. Simply put, these buses have a legal right to be on the road, and no amount of bullying can change that. 21 13;05 So the taxi operators would then come to you guys as an industry and say, these are the routes that you can operate on. And you can't operate on here. And you have to pay sort of protection fee for us not to attack you? 13;22 If you're willing to pay the ransom demand, then they will leave you alone. 22 VO “Ransom demand” is an appropriate description. This is like a hostage situation. Also known as security tax, money is paid to criminals so that they won’t attack you. It’s an arrangement very reminiscent of the mafia… a kind of warped insurance policy. 23 UPS 13;31 And this ransom demand is in the range of millions? Millions. Millions and millions. 24 VO It seems that there are only three ways to avoid violence: * Bus companies can agree, for example, to inflate their prices, which is illegal under the Competition Commission Act. This happened during the first wave of the Covid pandemic and companies were brought to justice for it. * Alternatively, they can cave in and pay the security tax; or, * steer clear of contested areas and routes. 25 VO In the 45 minutes we interviewed Ferreira, he received more bad news… 26 UPS 0;13 - 0;39 I actually can’t believe this. So while we’ve been doing this interview, Johann, two of your buses have been attacked… Yes, I believe so… (he reads from the message till 0;39) 27 VO Because of his refusal to cooperate with criminals, Eastern Cape towns like Dutywa, Butterworth, Tsomo, Cofimvaba and Ngcobo have become war zones for Intercape buses. 28 VO But the reign of terror has extended to other provinces as well… Terrifyingly, demonstrated by this CCTV footage of an Intercape bus leaving a depot in Cape Town. 29 VO SHOTS FIRED Bangikhaya Machana was shot three times. 30 VO His colleague who was sitting next to him, we’ll call him Dylan, recalls that fateful day… 31 UPS 4;55 When they start shooting what's going through your mind? 5;01 The intention was to shoot at the driver. He was struggling with the seatbelt. That is where he got shot. 06;14 The bullets was flying to this window… So we jumped up, over and he got into the sleeping compartment. 32 LINK I'm shocked how terrified these drivers were to talk to us... afraid that their attackers may come back and finish them off. They are bus drivers, not soldiers at war. 33 VO Machana underwent emergency surgery in a desperate bid to save his life. But the young father succumbed to his injuries only days later. 34 VO His grieving cousin, Koleke Machana, recalls that Machana’s love for driving buses took root when he was still just a child. 35 UPS 3;13 I remember they drove a bus without permission. So this is the reason the guy decided no, this child loves this. He took him to the Driving Academy. 36 VO Machana was the family breadwinner: husband and father to small girls. 37 VO Sadly, this mourning family’s trauma was far from over. When they arrived in an Intercape bus at Dutywa for the burial, minibus taxi drivers prevented them from entering the town. Their pleas fell on deaf ears and the taxi operators forced them to leave the area. 38 UPS 08:01 We just asked the driver please drive to this Mthatha you are instructed to drive to before we die here. We were scared. 39 VO Mthatha police escorted the bus back to Dutywa. 40 MEMORIAL SINGING 41 VO Intercape has intensified security at its depots and according to Ferreira, unmarked vehicles now have to escort buses on some routes. 42 VO Sadly, when buses are under siege, passengers also pay a price. On 29 April, an excited Pretty Nondabula, a mother of two, boarded a bus to visit family in the Eastern Cape. 43 VO She could not have known what would follow… 44 UPS 6;44 So you were shot? Yeah. Trying to go home? Yeah. 07;13 What did that feel like? 7;38 If you can put your leg on hot water - the hot, hot, hot, hot water when you're trying to put it like this. It's like that. 45 VO Traumatised and frantic to get home, Pretty’s leg was simply bandaged, before she got onto another bus to finish the trip. 46 VO Police in the Eastern Cape confirmed that they are prioritising investigations into the stoning of buses and intimidation by taxi operators. No arrests have been made yet. On screen: “The SAPS in the Eastern Cape is doing everything it can to prevent further occurrence of violent incidents aimed at buses.” In the Western Cape, a designated Taxi Violence Task Team and an Extortion Task Team are taking charge. They say their current investigations are linked to only one bus company, but the possibility that others are affected, cannot be ruled out. On screen: “Due to the sensitive nature of serious and violent crimes such as extortion, it is not possible to discuss the finer aspects of these cases on an open platform, as the identities of the victims must be protected.” 47 VO When asked if the issue is receiving attention at a national level, the SAPS National Office did not want to comment, merely saying that the investigation is ongoing. 48 VO Ferreira says he has opened more than 60 cases with the police. 49 VO In the meantime, Joseph bids a final farewell to his wife before every trip. 50 UPS SUBTITLES I ended up giving the Eastern Cape a name, calling it…what is the name of the country that is fighting with Russia? Ukraine I tell her that I’m going to Ukraine and we'll see if I come back. 51 VO Realising that a few thugs don’t define a whole industry, we tried to arrange an interview with the South African National Taxi Council, or SANTACO, but numerous WhatsApp messages, calls, SMS and emails to the official spokesperson stayed unanswered. But we cornered Minister Fikile Mbalula after an unrelated press briefing near Cape Town. 52 UPS 04;01 What do you do as a Minister of Transport when you have this one mode of transport being the taxi operators, intimidating and coming with arms, guns and taking passengers out? 04;24 Yes, you will know that from our side, we are dealing with a plethora of issues in terms of the taxi industry. And the chief amongst them is formalisation. And regulating. 53 VO This means the establishment of what he calls a “dedicated force”, focusing on violence in the taxi industry. 54 UPS 4;33 but at the present moment, with limited resources we've got our focus must shift to law enforcement 15;18 Where such happens, the minister got powers to close the roads, including MCs in the provinces, and that is what we'll do. Why aren’t you doing it yet? 05;15 Well, uh,we have done it where there's been an occurrence of that. 55 VO The Minister believes that a joint response by authorities, state departments and bus companies is needed. 56 UPS 05;47 Minister, to the family members of concerned every day when they keep hearing that they won't come back. What do you have to say? 5;23 I'm saying to them that from our side, the Ministry of Transport, we will do everything in our power to ensure that the criminals who are doing this work to book and then we would dedicate ourselves in the form of a team that will focus on this sort of violence. 57 VO All of which comes too late for Bangikhaya Machana and his bereaved family… PROMOS PROMO1 - 11 sec VO First e-hailing services, now long-distance buses… It seems like rogue taxi drivers will stop at nothing to clear their turf of other transport sectors - even if it leads to killings. PROMO 2 - 21 sec UPS 14;12 I thought it was a tyre exploding, so I checked my steering wheel and I felt if everything was still alright. SUBTITLES: I thought it was a tyre exploding, so I checked my steering wheel to feel if everything was still alright. I realised, no man, something is wrong here. VO Innocent bus drivers are getting injured and killed in a reign of terror led by taxi drivers. When will this stop? PROMO3 - 21 sec VO Long-distance bus travel is big business and highways from Johannesburg and Cape Town to small towns in the Eastern Cape, are prime real estate...now some minibus taxi drivers are staking their claim and they’ll stop at nothing to get the buses off the road... UPS 08:01 So we just asked the driver please drive to this Mthatha you are instructed to drive to before we die here. We were scared.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Actual footage of these attacks happening and people getting shot at or killed.
metadata.Summary: On 28 April 2022 an Intercape bus driver died days after being shot and critically wounded outside the Company’s Cape Town depot in what is part of a campaign of violence and extortion against the Long Distance Coach industry by rogue elements in the minibus taxi industry. The 35 year old victim leaves behind a wife and two daughters. In the space of just 13 months, there have been over 150 recorded violent incidents targeting Intercape,the country's largest and longest-standing bus company. A number of which have led to serious injury of industry employees and passengers on long distance coaches. The death of this latest Intercape employee comes as the Company has pleaded repeatedly for urgent government intervention to stop the campaign of violence. Intercape is not the only company being targeted, though, but they have been hit the hardest, because they are the biggest bus line driving long distance in the country. Also, they refuse to pay “protection money”. “Protection money” or “security tax” is money paid to ensure you will not be targeted by criminals. Thugs in the taxi industry try to extort long distance bus lines to either stay out of their “claimed” regions, or pay protection money to not fall victim to the attacks. SAPS and Nat Joints are supposed to be on board, but the attacks are only intensifying. More than 60 cases have been opened with the SAPS but the attacks have continued unabated at key pick-up points along routes and on the road, as well as outside Intercape headquarters in Cape Town where there have been two brazen shooting incidents, the latest of which was fatal. Intercape has now written to President Cyril Ramaphosa to act.
